title: Doubling the largest factor
why: Collatz-like; growth via Sophie Germain chains unbounded locally; cycle verified, no proof route.

title: Three halves of the largest factor
why: Collatz-like 3p/2 growth on primes; no contraction argument; cycle (3,5,8) verified.

title: Next-prime sums
why: From prime p>=7, (p+p')/2 is composite between consecutive primes so P(p+p')<=(p+p')/4<p; strictly decreasing.

title: Primes with equal binary and ternary digit sums
why: Spiegelhofer proved s2=s3 collisions for integers (2021); prime version needs joint two-base Mauduit-Rivat, open.

title: Möbius-signed Fibonacci
why: x_18=x_19=0 (computed), so sequence is identically zero afterward; limit is -infinity.

title: Linnik–Gallagher with seven-free primes
why: Needs Gallagher method with Maynard missing-digit primes; plausible but nontrivial; existing list has related seven-free items.

title: Turán density of a twisted triple system
why: F not 3-partite (forces 1,2 same part), so pi(F)>0; specific Turan density likely open, flag-algebra territory.

title: Codes with square distances
why: Only ~sqrt(n) allowed distances; Delsarte s-distance bound gives |C|<=sum_{i<=sqrt n}C(n,i)=2^{o(n)}, limit 0.

title: Twin-prime Nim
why: If finitely many twin primes, move set finite so P-positions periodic with positive density; density 0 implies twin primes infinite.

title: Bounded orbits for polynomial prime maps
why: Undecidability-type question on prime-factor dynamics; minor issue P(0),P(1) undefined when f(n) in {0,+-1}.

title: Resolution lower bound for square-sum colouring
why: chi(S_N) itself unknown; proof-complexity lower bound for structured number-theoretic graph, hard but well-posed.

title: Kneser graphs of square sums
why: Kneser upper bound N-2k+2 trivial; lower bound via alternation number/topological method likely tractable.

title: Extremal square-sum subgraphs
why: Upper O(N^{3/2}) trivial; S_N has ~N^2 log N C4s; Sidon subsets of squares give C4-free subgraphs; gap real.

title: Square-sum orderings avoiding progressions
why: Base Hamiltonian path problem treated as known; AP-avoidance constraint adds genuine difficulty.

title: Hindman with largest factors
why: Apply Hindman directly to colouring d(n)=c(P(n)); monochromatic IP set gives the claim.

title: Prime Nim with a doubling option
why: Computation: doubling changes almost nothing (only 155 below 200); "characterise" reduces to unstructured Prime Nim P-positions.

title: Sofa through a 120-degree corner
why: Special case of existing "Sofa for every angle" and overlaps "Obtuse sofa" (120 degree corridor).

title: Distance sets of the spectre tiling
why: Centres in finite-rank Z-module; distinct squared distances count via quadratic form values; doable but messy.

title: Isospectral monotiles
why: Open-ended construction; isospectrality via transplantation unlikely to fit aperiodic monotiles; very hard either way.

title: Zaremba with prime digits
why: Prime digits <=A imply Zaremba with constant A; also prime-alphabet dimension ~0.67 <5/6, beyond Bourgain-Kontorovich/Huang.

title: Equal-area hat dissection
why: Minimal dissection lower bounds are notoriously hard to prove; well-defined but likely intractable to certify.

title: Critical percolation on the hat tiling
why: p_c part duplicates existing "Percolation on the hat tiling"; Cardy for non-triangular lattice is famous universality problem.

title: Uniform spanning tree of the square-sum graph
why: Expected alpha=1/2 via expander UST results (Michaeli-Nachmias-Shalev); needs spectral gap of S_N, itself in existing list.

title: Hitting times of the random P-walk
why: n+-P(n) is divisible by P(n), so walk never reaches 1 (and hits 0 where P undefined); "chain above" undefined.

title: Loop-erased walk on the spectre tiling
why: Yadin-Yehudayoff (2011) give LERW->SLE2 on planar graphs once RW converges to BM; ergodic invariance principle covers spectre.

title: Hitting probability for 2P(n)+1 random variant
why: Recurrence needs control of P(2p+-1) distribution, like Elliott-Halberstam-level input; simulations hit 5 often.

title: The shift-3 prime map
why: Collatz-like; twin-prime-like pairs n,n+3 make orbits grow; cycles verified to 20000.

title: Four fates of P(n)+P(n+1)+1
why: Collatz-like; four fates verified to 20000; no contraction mechanism.

title: Keller maps with two-point fibres in dimension 3
why: Degree-2 field extension is Galois; Campbell (1973): Keller maps with Galois extension are invertible. Also duplicates "Two-to-one Keller maps".

title: Prime Nim Grundy values are unbounded
why: Same as existing "Unbounded Prime Nim".

title: Seven-free Carmichael numbers
why: Same as existing "Seven-free Carmichael numbers".

title: Seven-free square sums of two squares
why: Heuristically exceptional set infinite (reps r(n) small vs 0.81^digits); proving it still needs constructing explicit families.

title: Twin width of square-sum graphs
why: Easy if S_N is K_{t,t}-free (bounded tww + K_tt-free => bounded degeneracy), but K_{t,t} in squares is open.

title: Clique minors in the prime-sum graph
why: n/sqrt(log n) is trivial edge-count upper bound; random heuristic gives n/log n, so claimed lower bound likely false/very hard.
